submission.justification: Module-D3 (large-area light guide with thin bonded dichroic filter) at 30% wall coverage gives the highest light collection of the three designs in the current simulation: 51.3 PE/MeV, versus 38.9 PE/MeV for Module-D2 and 24.1 PE/MeV for Module-D1 at the same coverage (100,000 events each). 30% is the upper limit of the allowed range; the 2025 summary reports light yield rising roughly as coverage^0.8, so the maximum coverage is the best choice for the goal. Feedthroughs are sufficient for 30% coverage (meeting notes 2026-01-20), and cold electronics are validated for all candidate designs. Robustness is the main open point: no project document assesses the long-term reliability of the bonded dichroic filter in liquid argon, and inaccessibility after fill makes this a real risk. Before the Q3 design freeze, the filter bond should be qualified with cryogenic thermal-cycling and immersion tests. If D3 fails that qualification, D2 (38.9 PE/MeV at 30%, WLS bar with SiPM readout) is the fallback.
